paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Faithfulness to God and faithfulness to people are the same road. Malachi starts with "Do we not all have one Father? Did not one God create us?" (Malachi 2:10). Then he asks why they break faith with one another, and he names Judah's sin: marrying the daughter of a foreign god (Malachi 2:10-11).

Look at what he says about the offerings. The people were covering the altar with tears, but the LORD no longer received their offerings gladly (Malachi 2:13). I think that hurts to hear, because the weeping was real. Still, a gift on the altar can't cover for a promise broken at home, and the LORD was a witness between each man and the wife of his youth (Malachi 2:14).

So what does it mean for you, baker? If you're married, your marriage is a covenant that the LORD Himself witnesses, and He tells the men, "do not break faith with the wife of your youth" (Malachi 2:15). He says, "For I hate divorce," says the LORD, the God of Israel (Malachi 2:16). Guard your spirit, keep faith with your spouse, and keep your heart true to the LORD instead of drifting to another god (Malachi 2:11).
